title: Are HoLEP Surgical Videos on YouTube Biased and Misleading or Are They Leading the Industry?
screen_reason: Content analysis of 117 English-language YouTube videos on holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP). Videos were rated for degree of misinformation on a 1-5 Likert scale (none/low/moderate/high/extreme) with reference to EAU guideline evidence by two independent endourologists (third adjudicator), and the distribution is reported as shares of videos: “16.2% had extreme- or high-degree misinformation” (Table 1: Severe 0.8%, High 11.9%, Moderate 33.3%, Low 32.4%, None 12.8%). That is a share of items judged for accuracy against an external ground truth (guideline concordance), so CONTENT; the accompanying DISCERN/GQS/JAMA/PEMAT instruments are coded QUALITY.

estimates.ground_truth_detail: “The videos included in the study were watched by two independent surgeons, both specialized in endourology. In case of inconsistent evaluation between the two surgeons (non-matching results), a third physician evaluated the videos.” Accuracy standard: EAU non-oncology guidelines on management of non-neurogenic male LUTS. No kappa reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: The keywords “HoLEP”, “laser enucleation” and “prostate enucleation” were used to conduct a search on YouTube (http://www.youtube.com) on December 16, 2020, without using any search filter. ... A total of 1,416 videos were screened, and 1,156 videos were excluded from the study because they were non-English, irrelevant, or non-audio. Further 143 videos were excluded due to duplication. Thus, the number of videos that were eligible was 117
estimates.notes: ADJUDICATOR NOTE — the paper's numbers do not reconcile. (1) The extracted 16.2% is stated verbatim in the Discussion but cannot be reproduced from Table 1: Severe 1 + High 14 = 15/117 = 12.8%; 16.2% implies 19/117. (2) The Table 1 misinformation categories sum to 107, not 117 (1+14+39+38+15), so 10 videos are unaccounted for. (3) The upload-source subtotals also disagree with the text: Results says n=94 (77.7%) healthcare providers, Table 2 says n=90 (and 90/117 = 76.9%); Discussion says commercial bias in 55.7% while Table 1 says 66 (56.4%). I kept the paper's own verbatim overall figure per R8 rather than summing Table 1 categories myself (a cross-category sum R8 forbids); a value-checker should expect 12.8% from the table. borderline=true because the numerator is a Likert DEGREE of misinformation rather than a binary false/not-false judgement, though it is anchored to EAU guideline evidence, which meets the CONTENT test (guideline concordance). Also note the group contrast reported in the abstract (high-degree misinformation 5.5% in healthcare-provider videos vs 33.3% in commercial/for-profit videos) — a moderator split of this same estimate, not extracted as separate rows since it is not a country/platform/measure split and the paper's headline overall figure is the 16.2%.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: (a) the GQS distribution (GQS 1 = 0.9%, GQS 2 = 12.8%, GQS 3 = 23.9%, GQS 4 = 49.6%, GQS 5 = 12.8%) and the JAMA group split (JAMA <2 = 75.5% / 74.1% by group) — further QUALITY-instrument distributions, redundant with the DISCERN QUALITY row kept above; (b) “commercial bias was present in 55.7%” (Table 1: 66, 56.4%) — commercial bias is not a truth/falsity judgement, so not misinformation under this review's definition; (c) median DISCERN, GQS, JAMA, PEMAT understandability/actionability and misinformation-SCORE values (medians only, e.g. misinformation score median 3.00) — scale means/medians with no share, no row per §3; (d) “Absent/Exist” shares for discussion of alternative treatments (63.2%), side effects (54.7%), surgical benefits (95.7%) — completeness, not falsity; (e) the by-upload-source misinformation shares (5.5% vs 33.3% high-degree) — a moderator split of the extracted estimate; (f) figures the paper cites from other studies (e.g. Fode et al. PEMAT medians). No time series and no concentration statistics are reported.

rob.design: Cross-sectional YouTube content analysis. Search of three keywords (“HoLEP”, “laser enucleation”, “prostate enucleation”) on 16 December 2020 with no search filter, browsers cleared and location disabled; 1,416 videos screened, 1,156 excluded (non-English, irrelevant, non-audio), 143 duplicates excluded, 117 eligible; videos <4 minutes and non-English excluded. Two independent endourology surgeons rated every video, with a third physician adjudicating disagreements; instruments were a 1-5 Likert misinformation scale anchored to EAU guideline evidence, plus DISCERN, GQS, JAMA, PEMAT and a commercial-bias assessment (Cornish & Leist). No inter-rater reliability coefficient reported. Authors note the single-platform, single-time-point and English-only limitations. Several reported counts and percentages are mutually inconsistent (see notes).
